newsitem.title: UK: Malaysia Equity says Peregrine misleading.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Equity says Peregrine misleading.

text.p: The beleaguered $200 million Malaysia Equity Fund Ltd alleged in a statement that Peregrine Securities (UK) Ltd is misleading shareholders with its proposals to restructure the fund.

"Peregrine has made a number of misleading statements that your board believes have been misleading to shareholders while professing to support the appointment of independent advisors," the fund's chairman Kiyoshi Matsuba said in a letter to shareholders ahead of a key vote on the fund on September 24.
In June, Peregrine announced proposals to open-end the fund to narrow the discount to net asset value at which shares trade.
The average discount in the 12 months before Peregrine made its offer was 17.2 percent.
The fund has responded with its own open-ending proposals which it says would save shareholders $2.0 million and stand a better chance of getting through regulatory hurdles in Malaysia.
However, Peregrine dismissed the Malaysia Equity Fund's claims as a desperate attempt to influence the shareholder meeting.
"This is a last ditch effort; we put out our proposals on July 23 and a lot of shareholders have already given their votes," said Nicholas Paris of Peregrine.
Malaysia Equity says that the Peregrine open ending proposals, for which Peregrine would receive a fee of one percent of assets, ignore the rights of minority shareholders.

"While acknowledging the significant importance of the views of the majority shareholders, the board believes that it would have failed in its duty to protect the rights of minority shareholders and competently examine the options available to the fund," Matsuba said.
He also accused Peregrine of strong-arm tactics in pushing for agreement to its proposals before the board had a chance to consider a response.

"Your board believes that the Peregrine proposals are in the interest of one group of shareholders and their advisor, Peregrine, and not in the interests of the fund and its shareholders as a whole," he added.
Peregrine dismissed Matsuba's statament and remains adamant that it will carry the vote.
"We have always had more than 50 percent of shareholders on our side and we believe it is now closer to 70 percent," said Paris.
